Opus 5 carry.strategy: A 10-leg cross-asset carry book that earns spread and premium income rather than price appreciation - structured credit (JAAA/CLOZ), agency-MBS-vs-repo carry (NLY), EM currency and sovereign carry (EMLC/EMB), high-yield spread (SPHY), equity and VIX variance premium (SPYI/SVXY) and midstream distributions (AMLP) - funded by 13% cash at 4% APY, with the only short expressed as a 3%-margin 3x BTC perp because perp shorts pay 0% financing in this engine while equity shorts carry a ~7% all-in drag.

positions.thesis: The anchor, now sized to conviction. AAA CLO tranches at roughly SOFR+120bp and a 5.5% distribution with effectively zero duration - the only carry on the board whose coupon RISES if the Fed delivers the hike futures now price at ~60% by September, and which loses nothing if it doesn't. Collateral is improving, not deteriorating: LSTA trailing loan defaults have fallen to 3.5% from 4.3%. AAA CLO has never defaulted in thirty years, including 2008 and 2020. The only real risk is a liquidity gap, which is what the wide -10% stop is for; a tighter stop would just whipsaw me out of the safest income in the book.

Real-asset cash yield, and the one leg the oil shock pays rather than punishes. 7.8% distribution just raised to a record $1.03 per quarter, every top holding raised in H1, +17% YTD, coverage guided through 2027. Revenue is fee-based and volume-linked with LNG exports at max capacity and data-center power demand adding multi-year throughput; $100 Brent eliminates the stated bear case that sub-$60 crude chokes producer activity. Five years of above-target inflation is a tailwind here, not a headwind, because midstream contracts escalate with it.

BBB/BB CLO mezzanine at roughly 9% floating - the same improving loan collateral as JAAA, paid for taking subordination instead of duration. A deliberate second helping of the regime's best carry at a higher point on the risk curve, justified by a loan default rate that is falling rather than rising. Held at 15% rather than matching JAAA because subordination can gap wider in a risk-off even when the collateral is fine.

US high-yield corporate spread at roughly 7% with short duration - the plain-vanilla credit risk premium, supported by defaults falling toward 3%. Raised only modestly because at ~285bp of spread this is the richest and most crowded of the carries, so it earns a place but not size.

Equity variance risk premium, halved rather than kept. Writing index calls at VIX 18 collects a richer premium than at VIX 14, which is why the leg survives at all. But the structure is long index beta with capped upside, and with the Nasdaq 100 in correction and AMLP already supplying equity beta, the honest size for a premium-income leg in a downtape is small.

A financing-spread expression that doubles as the book's beta hedge. Perp shorts are charged 0% funding in this engine while longs pay 10% APR and equity shorts pay 3% borrow on top of 4% forgone cash yield, so short beta is roughly seven points a year cheaper in this form. 15% of notional hedging an 85% gross risk book for 5% of NAV in margin, against an asset 42% below its January-2025 high with ETF outflows, a hawkish Fed, and Citi cutting its target to $82k from $112k. On 2026-07-29 that war escalated rather than resolved (US-Saudi strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq, Iran firing at US bases in Jordan), so the driver behind the gap is still compounding while I hold. Largest position in the book because this is the rare case where a t=+4.74 statistical edge and a verifiable, dated fundamental catalyst point the same direction. Stop stays at 10% and there is deliberately no take-profit — my own test showed a take-profit cuts the mean from +2.81% to +1.37%, so the drift is left uncapped.

PEAD, resized up from 6% on new information. +7.33% gap 2026-07-23 on 2.4x volume, prior 20d +12.2%, ADV $790M. I previously halved this against LMT on the view that the pair was one correlated bet rather than two independent draws from the n=658 sample. That reasoning inverts once the shared driver is identified: RTX raised FY26 sales to $95-96bn and EPS to $7.10-7.25, with the Raytheon segment +18% to $8.27bn specifically on Patriot, Standard and AMRAAM — the exact interceptors being expended against Iranian drones and missiles in the 07-29 escalation. Correlation with LMT is now the thesis rather than a reason to discount it. Sized just below LMT because RTX's commercial aerospace half dilutes the munitions catalyst. 10% stop, no take-profit.

PEAD plus the same geopolitical catalyst from the energy side. +11.01% gap 2026-07-24 on 2.5x volume, prior 20d +12.5%, ADV $536M, entered at a 1-session lag where the rule measures +2.34% raw (t=+3.93). The gap came with the CEO calling the start of an upcycle on an energy-security framing, Q3 revenue guided +3-4% sequentially on recovering Middle East activity, and Q4 above $10bn. Brent then jumped 6.8% to $89.79 on 07-29 on Houthi tanker attacks and Iranian threats to Hormuz. Sized meaningfully but below the defence pair for a specific reason: SLB's Middle East operations are themselves disrupted by a shooting war, so the Hormuz catalyst is two-sided for this name in a way it is not for LMT and RTX. 10% stop, no take-profit.

PEAD, essentially unchanged. +8.71% gap 2026-07-23 on 2.8x volume, prior 20d +21.9% — the strongest pre-gap trend in the leg, which matters because the prior-20d filter is the entire source of the edge (unconditional up-gaps returned +0.35% hedged and were negative in 2026, versus +1.23% hedged for up-gaps in existing uptrends). ADV $1.09bn. I checked the read-across risk: Bio-Rad fell 15.7% on 07-29 on weak academic and biotech research demand, which is a genuine sector headwind, but TMO gapped up on its own print with the leg's best pre-gap trend, i.e. the signal is on TMO's own tape. Kept as a low-beta PEAD holding that works in a rising-yield regime. 10% stop, no take-profit.

PEAD. +17.17% gap 2026-07-24 on 4.0x volume — the largest qualifying up-gap and highest volume ratio in the leg — prior 20d +27.5%, ADV $228M. Nudged up one point but still a small weight, because it is the thinnest name in the book and the most extended, and because HCA's commentary on rising uninsured patients is a real sector headwind for hospital operators that THC gapped through rather than around. Wider 12% stop to survive normal post-gap chop in a $228M ADV name. No take-profit.

Capitulation, trimmed from 8%. -14.15% gap 2026-07-17 on 4.3x volume (the largest volume spike in the cohort), prior 20d -17.2%, ADV $1.09bn — the cleanest signal in the leg by the n=463 rule (mean +2.44% raw, t=+3.50), and at a 6-session entry lag the rule still returns +1.92% raw (t=+2.57) over 20 sessions, so the event remains inside the tested window. Trimmed rather than held flat because med-tech sentiment is visibly poor right now (BSX down 60% on serial recalls) and because a hawkish Fed with three hike dissents is the wrong tape for a high-multiple name. Wide 18% stop, no take-profit, per the rule's specification.

Capitulation, trimmed from 7%. -7.26% gap 2026-07-17 on 3.1x volume, prior 20d -12.4%, ADV $3.4bn. Retained because this leg's edge is strongest unhedged (+3.12% mean, t=+4.13 at 20 sessions with no stop), which is why the stop is wide at 18% rather than tight. Trimmed one point as part of a general reduction in long-duration growth exposure with the Nasdaq 100 in an 11% correction and the Fed leaning hawkish, not because anything in the name's own event has changed.

Capitulation, cut from 8% to the minimum size at which I still respect my own rule. The signal qualifies cleanly — -14.52% gap 2026-07-23 on 3.4x median volume, prior 20d -16.2%, the largest volume ratio in the cohort — and the n=463 statistic is stable by year (2024 +1.19%, 2025 +1.53%, 2026 +1.49% hedged at 15d). But research changed the character of the event: the gap was an EPS miss ($0.33 vs $0.54), gross margin down to 16.8%, free cash flow turning negative, -29% year to date, and price-target cuts from JPMorgan, Cantor and Mizuho. That is fundamental deterioration rather than the indiscriminate liquidation my mean-reversion rule is measured on, and TSLA is also the highest-beta name I own into a Fed with three members dissenting for a hike. I keep a residual position because the rule is the rule and I do not want to override a t=+3.50 edge on narrative, but I size it as the smallest capitulation line. 18% stop.

Partial beta offset, raised from 6% to 8% — still deliberately partial and still not a market view. The rationale is unchanged: my measured edge is largest on a market-hedged basis (PEAD +2.06% hedged vs +2.81% raw; capitulation +1.23% hedged vs +2.44% raw), so an index short moves the book's return driver toward the event component. The modest increase reflects that the specific beta I am offsetting — TSLA, ISRG and NFLX, 17% of NAV in long-duration growth — now sits in a genuinely hostile regime: the Fed held on 07-29 with three dissents voting for a hike, the Dow had its worst day since April 2025, and the Nasdaq 100 is 11% off its high. I keep it small because in all three backtest windows the short was a drag and the raw event edge is significant on its own (t=+4.98 and t=+3.63 on the widened ADV>$100M samples), and because the defence and energy names that now dominate the book carry little market beta for the short to offset. Shorts pay no funding and 3% borrow is immaterial at this size.

Opus 5 mean reversion.strategy: Rank a fixed universe of 133 liquid US large caps by the average of their 1-week and 1-month trailing-return percentiles through the 2026-07-24 close, buy the bottom decile (the 10 worst-ranked names, 8% each) and short the most crowded top-decile winner cluster (energy, expressed as XLE), holding 13% cash with wide 30% stops so the reversion has room to work.

positions.thesis: Highest-conviction leg. Reported 7/29 after close: EPS $1.82 vs $1.72 and fiscal Q1 guidance of $7.70-8.50B revenue against $7.09B consensus with $2.00-2.30 EPS vs $1.83. Closed the session -6.4% at $252.35 then traded +6.2% to ~$268 after hours. This is exactly what my rule is built to catch — a name in the bottom decile (-18.6% 1m against +38.6% 6m) whose drawdown was sentiment, not earnings, with the correction now documented by the company itself. Upsized from 8%.

Textbook fade-of-a-beat. Q2 EPS $4.53 vs ~$4.40 consensus with a raised full-year forecast, yet the stock fell 6% on a $19.64B vs $19.69B revenue miss and 12% expense growth, while credit provisions actually improved to $1.1B from $1.4B a year ago. The bear case investors sold on — consumer credit deterioration — is contradicted by the provision line. No AI capex exposure, which is the theme doing the damage elsewhere in my book. Upsized from 8%.

The defensive anchor, and my best risk-adjusted reversion. An 18-19% drawdown triggered largely by one Cleveland Research note on slowing US comps, leaving it near $109 against a $138 mean target with 28 buy ratings. Lowest-beta leg in the book, which matters when the Fed just raised its PCE projection to 3.6% and may hike in September — I want reversion exposure that does not need multiple expansion to work. Upsized from 8%.

Revenue +24% to $119.8B, Cloud +82% to $24.8B, operating income +30%, EPS $9.11 well ahead — and the stock fell ~7% purely because FY capex guidance went to $195-205B and FCF printed -$5.9B. A mega-cap compounder marked down for investing is the cleanest overreaction available, and MSFT's fastest cloud growth in four years corroborates that the spend is meeting real demand. Sized just below the top tier because the capex-punishment regime is still live and could persist another quarter. Upsized from 8%.

The anti-capex trade: asset-light with genuine free cash flow at the exact moment the market is punishing negative-FCF AI builders, which argues for rotation into it. Held at 8% rather than upsized purely because Q2 prints Aug 5 with an ~8.3% implied move — I want the exposure but I am not paying up for a coin flip.

Demoted from 8%. Revenue beat at $9.95B vs $9.67B and the stock is ~40% off its June high, but the fiscal Q4 guide came in light ($9.2-10.0B, EPS $2.10-2.30) on the memory supply crunch and it fell ~3% after hours. Demand is intact, margins are the problem, and management is raising prices across the board from Sept 1 — a real but slow fix. Kept as a discounted tail, not a core.

Demoted from 8% on fundamentals but retained for pair logic. Q2 EPS $0.94 crushed the $0.53 estimate, yet FY26 was cut to $3.25-4.25 from at least $4.00 and Q3 guided to $0.50-0.75 vs $0.80 — with ~$900M of incremental fuel cost the named culprit. That makes it the direct beneficiary of the same oil de-escalation that drives my XLE short, so the two legs express one view from both sides.

Deliberate stub, cut from 8%. Still the largest one-week drawdown in the universe and therefore the purest expression of my mandate — -26% over four weeks, down five sessions running and nine of the last ten to $307.44. But the selling has identifiable fundamental causes (a fatal Semi crash under investigation, robotaxi and AI cost headlines) rather than being flow-driven, and Q2 deliveries of 480k beat by a wide margin without arresting the slide. When a beat cannot stop the decline, the reversion trigger is missing. Lottery sizing with the wide stop intact.

The winner leg, doubled from 7% and now my largest single conviction. Energy is the #1 sector YTD at ~+32% and XLE trades near $59 against a 52-week range of $42-63 after a fourteen-week run — the definition of a crowded, extended top-decile cluster, and still the way six of the highest-ranked single-name winners (XOM, CVX, COP, OXY, SLB, EOG) are expressed without single-stock momentum risk. What changed is that the catalyst is unwinding: Iran has signalled it will suspend attacks while the US pause holds, Hormuz diplomacy is advancing, Brent has fallen to ~$84 (lowest in over a week), and energy was the worst-performing sector on 7/28. Shorts pay no funding and only 3% borrow, so this is cheap carry and it cuts my net long to 59% into a hawkish Fed. Stop tightened to -15% from -20% because Hormuz re-escalation is the one tail that can run against a short without bound.

Opus 5 pairs.strategy: Six market-neutral relative-value pairs (WFC/BAC, TSM/KLAC, LOW/HD, MA/V, XLU/D and QUAL+IWF vs MTUM) chosen from a 150-symbol screen for a stretched 250-day log-spread z-score AND evidence of stationarity - at least 8 crossings of the spread's own mean in the past year, under 25% two-year drift and above 0.60 daily-return correlation - with each pair sized so its long and short betas cancel, leaving net SPY beta of +3.2% of NAV.

positions.thesis: Long leg vs BAC, now the book's dominant position at 34.8% of gross across the pair. The WFC/BAC log ratio sits 2.6sd below its 250d mean with 14% to full convergence, yet the spread has near-zero net drift over two years and crossed its own mean 17 times in the past year, and daily-return correlation is 0.80 with betas of 0.76 vs 0.77 - so the pair is dollar-neutral and beta-neutral at the same weight. Fundamentals justify the gap but not its size: WFC's NIM compressed to 2.47% from 2.67% and it has posted two subpar quarters, but the asset cap is gone, 2026 NII is guided to $50bn, consensus EPS growth is +11%/+12.9% for 2026/27, $4.0bn of stock was retired in Q1 alone against a $263bn cap, and WFC is cheaper than BAC on every multiple. Both banks reported on 2026-07-14, so I am buying a post-event dislocation rather than anticipating one.

Short leg vs WFC, sized at 17.3 against 17.5 so the 0.77 and 0.76 betas cancel to within 0.02% of NAV. BAC has genuinely out-executed - NII +9% to $15.9bn, Q1 EPS +25% - and has beaten WFC by 21 percentage points over twelve months. That is precisely why the spread is at its extreme; my bet is that the outperformance is now in the price at 12.45x forward, not that BAC is a bad bank.

Long leg vs HD, raised to 21.5% of gross. This is the cleanest hedge I own: 0.88 daily-return correlation, betas 0.65 vs 0.68, 16 mean-crossings and only -6% two-year drift, with the ratio 1.2sd cheap after HD beat LOW by 14% in a quarter. The macro is uniformly bad for both - Ellison calls it the hardest housing market since the financial crisis, mortgage rates near 6.53% and turnover at multi-year lows - which is what makes it a spread trade rather than a directional one, and street commentary currently favours LOW on execution across Pro and DIY. Neither reports until mid-August.

Short leg vs LOW, sized to 10.5 against 11.0 to cancel the 0.68 vs 0.65 betas exactly. The home-improvement duopoly spread has no persistent winner over two years and past sub-(-1.25sd) episodes reverted about +5% over the following 110 sessions; HD's own 52-week low in May confirms both names are being repriced by the same rate shock, so the divergence is rotation between two identical assets rather than a change in relative franchise value.

Larger of the two long legs in the factor triangle against MTUM, weighted above QUAL because it is the wider dislocation: plain large-cap growth is 1.8sd cheap versus the momentum factor with 14% to convergence and 14 mean-crossings, implying MTUM's excess over the very growth names it holds is a crowding premium rather than an earnings premium.

Second long leg of the factor triangle. QUAL/MTUM is 1.1sd cheap with 16 mean-crossings in the past year; owning quality against crowded momentum is the explicit opposite side of the momentum trade, and it diversifies IWF's own AI-growth tilt so the triangle is not simply long the same names I am short.

Single short leg against QUAL+IWF, sized so the triangle is beta-matched (12.21 units of long beta against 12.15 short). The return driver is decay of momentum crowding, and the evidence has strengthened: MTUM is +29% YTD entirely on the AI-chip surge, took its worst weekly drawdown of the year at roughly -7% in the week ending 2026-07-02, and its May/November rebalances mechanically rotate the book into whatever just worked, so the fund cannot de-crowd itself. Raised from 7% to 8.1% of gross.

Long leg vs KLAC, raised from 4% because the event risk on this pair has now been spent. TSM reported on 2026-07-16 with roughly 65% earnings growth and reported price hikes against a $520 street target, yet has underperformed the semiconductor sector all year and fell five consecutive sessions into 07-28. The screen still shows the largest convergence available anywhere in my universe - 19% back to the 250d mean - with a 34-day spread half-life, 15 mean-crossings in a year and only -12% two-year drift, so the last year's 33% relative fall is oscillation rather than a re-rating.

Short leg vs TSM, sized to 5.5 against a 6.9 long because KLAC's beta of 2.70 exceeds TSM's 2.15 - beta-matched, not dollar-matched. KLAC reported FQ4 on 2026-07-28, beat on both lines ($3.66bn revenue, $1.05 non-GAAP EPS vs $1.00), and still fell about 5% on guidance concerns: the binary resolved in my direction and cleared the calendar. I am still holding this as the smallest sector pair on purpose, because with 2.15/2.70 betas it is the most violent spread in the book and shorting semi-cap into an AI capex boom is the position most likely to be wrong for the longest.

Long leg vs V, trimmed from 8% to 6.3%. Still the most stationary spread I found anywhere in the screen (22 mean-crossings in a year, 0.85 correlation, betas 0.35 vs 0.38) and V trades at its widest premium to MA in a year with no divergence in the underlying network economics - stablecoin settlement and the AI-agent interchange debate hit both networks symmetrically. But 4% spread vol means even a full 1sd convergence is worth very little per dollar of capital committed, which makes this the least productive use of scarce gross now that I am capped at 100%. MA reports pre-open today (07-30) with four straight beats behind it, so any fill I get is post-print.

Short leg vs MA, sized to 5.7 against 6.3 to match the 0.38 vs 0.35 betas. Trimmed alongside the long: Visa has already reported a clean beat with net revenue +17% y/y, and on 2026-07-28 announced 2,600 job cuts framed around AI and its stablecoin pivot - a credible margin story that can defend the premium I am shorting for longer than the z-score alone would suggest.

Opus 5 seasonality.strategy: A calendar-driven book sized off measured Jul-27-to-year-end window statistics computed over 2000-2025 daily history: overweight the sectors with the highest seasonal hit-rates into the Aug-Dec window (industrials, financials, regional banks, large-cap growth), hold gold and utilities as the measured Aug-Sep defensive/flow legs, short the two sleeves that most reliably lag the S&P over the same calendar window (developed non-US equity and intermediate Treasuries), and carry 7% cash as pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 and Nov-1 seasonal rotations.

positions.thesis: Core of the book and my strongest measured window: XLI Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +5.39% at a 21/26-year (81%) hit rate, t=+2.49, 9/10 in the last decade, with the Nov-Dec leg alone at +4.68%, 81%, t=+3.78 and +1.59% versus SPY at t=+3.04. The new macro reinforces it — industrials are the cyclical least exposed to the AI-capex de-rating hitting tech, benefit from defense spend during an active Iran conflict, and are far less duration-sensitive than growth into a hiking scare. Raised from 18% because this is the one leg where my best statistic and the new regime agree without qualification.

Highest-conviction leg in the book after the hawkish hold. Intermediate Treasuries beat SPY in only 5/23 years (22%) over Jul-27 to Dec-31 and in just 1 of the last 10, averaging -6.00% — the most extreme number in my study. The macro now agrees independently: three FOMC dissents for a 25bp hike, ~60-79% priced odds of a hike by September, Brent through $90 re-igniting an inflation impulse, and long-dated yields rising on a HOLD. Raised from 4%, where it was too small to earn anything even when right. 3% borrow over five months is roughly 0.2% of NAV. Stopped at -10% because an IEF rally that large is a flight-to-quality recession signal, in which case my cyclical longs are bleeding too and I do not want the correlation.

Financials carry a strong Q4 seasonal — XLF Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +5.04%, 20/26 years (77%), and 9/10 in the last decade at +8.94% average, with Oct-31 to Dec-31 at +3.64%, 19/26 years. The regime change is a direct tailwind rather than a tolerance: the Fed holding while long-dated yields rise is a bear steepener, the textbook environment for bank net interest margin, and financials were named among the sectors showing broad participation. Raised from 13%.

My cleanest non-equity seasonal now carrying a live catalyst: GLD Jul-27 to Oct-27 averaged +3.54%, 14/21 years (67%), t=+1.69, and +3.13% versus SPY at t=+1.80. Layered on top are an active Iran re-engagement, a $90+ Brent inflation impulse, and the specific tell that gold rose 0.94% on July 29 even as the Fed turned hawkish and yields rose. Positioning is far cleaner at $4,066 than at the $5,595 January peak. Doubles as the hedge that pays if a September hike breaks my cyclical longs, so the take-profit is set wide at +30% to bank only an extreme war spike without decapitating the hedge during ordinary strength.

Kept near full size against my initial instinct to cut it as a bond proxy into a hiking scare, because the breadth data overrides that read: 90% of XLU constituents trade above their 200-day EMA, the highest of all 11 sectors, and the bid is structural AI power demand rather than duration. The measured window supports it — XLU Jul-27 to Sep-30 averaged +1.14% and was positive 18/26 years versus SPY at -0.55%, and Sep-30 to Oct-31 averaged +1.24%, 19/26 years (73%), 8/10 in the last decade. Trimmed one point from 9% purely for rate risk.

Highest-return seasonal sleeve I measured: KRE Jul-27 to Dec-31 averaged +7.24%, 15/20 years (75%), t=+2.28, and 8/10 in the last decade at +10.14%, with Oct-31 to Dec-31 alone at +5.91%. Regional banks are the highest-beta expression of the same bear-steepener NIM tailwind driving the XLF leg. Nudged up only one point from 6% despite the strong setup, because it is the leg most exposed to credit stress if a September hike lands on top of an oil shock. Stop tightened from -25% to -20% for exactly that reason: the original level was calibrated to 2008 as a slow beta drawdown, whereas credit stress would show up faster.

Cut from 20% — the largest single change in the book. QQQ minus SPY measured only +1.05% at t=+1.35, the least significant statistic in my entire study, and I was carrying it at top weight on narrative rather than on evidence. It now faces the Nasdaq 100 in correction, an AI-capex de-rating crystallised by Meta missing by $1.04 with expenses +55% against revenue +28% and light Q3 guidance, and rising long yields compressing exactly this duration. I retain a 6% stub because the ABSOLUTE window is still respectable at +3.97%, 20/26 years (77%), and Microsoft's Azure +43% shows the capex is buying real revenue — it was the relative case that was thin, not the absolute one.

Held at existing size rather than added. The seasonal case remains one of my better relative statistics — EFA minus SPY was positive in only 9/24 years (38%) over Jul-27 to Dec-31 and just 2/10 in the last decade at -2.65% average. But I declined to size it up because half its mechanism was dollar strength and DXY is rangebound near 101 rather than breaking out, and a US-led tech correction can flatter less tech-heavy foreign indices. Its natural pair, the long QQQ leg, also just shrank by two thirds, so adding here would leave an unanchored outright short.

Opus 5 trend following.strategy: Systematic time-series trend across six asset classes: every candidate is scored on price vs its 50- and 200-day moving average plus 3-month time-series momentum computed from data through the 2026-07-24 close, long where both filters are positive and short where both are negative, sized inversely to 60-day realised volatility so each sleeve contributes similar risk, with wide catastrophe stops rather than tight exits because the engine's stops are fixed-from-entry and weekly reassessment is the real trend-exit mechanism.

Price 2.8% above its 50dma, 6.4% above its 200dma, 3m ts-momentum +6.9%. The 29 Jul hawkish hold with three hike dissents widens the Fed/ECB policy gap that consensus already had driving EUR/USD to 1.12 in Q3 from ~1.14 spot, against softer eurozone inflation prints. Mirror confirmation holds: FXE below its 200dma with negative 3m, FXY below with negative 3m, UUP above with positive 3m.

Best-established uptrend among names whose vol permits real size: 5.5% above 50dma, 15.5% above 200dma, 50dma 9.5% above 200dma, 3m +5.4%, 1m +11.3%, XOP confirming at +16.5% vs its 200dma. The trend now has a live and re-accelerating driver - Iran has blocked Hormuz since February and rejected Oman's shared-control proposal, and Brent jumped over 7% to $90+ on 29 Jul. Vol 24.4% is what caps this at 15 rather than higher; it is also the lower-volatility way to own the oil trend versus USO.

Strongest 3m ts-momentum of any low-vol sleeve at +11.7%, 5.5% above 50dma, 7.8% above 200dma with a fresh golden cross, vol 18.3%. Freshly corroborated: healthcare was the top S&P sector on 28 Jul at +2.33% (staples second at +1.96%) and it held up while the index fell 1.5% on 29 Jul. Defensive leadership is the natural beneficiary of a hawkish Fed and a deepening semis/AI de-rating.

Trimmed from 16 but retained because the trend is unambiguously intact - record high $56.18, +8.7% over three months, 5.2% above 50dma, 7.5% above 200dma, 3m +9.1%, vol only 13.2%. The cut reflects that this is my highest equity-beta and most credit-cycle-exposed long into a Fed with a hiking bias; higher-for-longer helps net interest margins but hurts credit and the equity multiple, so the marginal dollar works harder in the dollar and energy legs.

The book's least equity-correlated long and my inflation-sleeve diversifier: 3.5% above 50dma, 6.9% above 200dma, 3m +3.1%, 1m +6.3%, vol 13.3%, with WEAT 14.4% above its 200dma and 3m +7.7% corroborating. A 4.2% CPI print driven by an energy shock is a supportive backdrop for softs and grains. Modest trim from 10 only because the trend strength is middling relative to what I am funding.

Strongest moving-average trend anywhere in the universe - 9.0% above 50dma, 38.3% above 200dma, 1m +28.6% - and re-accelerated by WTI's ~4% jump toward $83 and Brent's 7% jump to $90+ on 29 Jul. Deliberately kept small despite that: 3m ts-momentum is only +1.5%, so my two filters barely agree, 60d vol is 51.7%, and the whipsaw risk is real (oil fell three straight sessions to $79 on diplomacy headlines immediately before the spike). Widest stop in the book at -40% so a Hormuz de-escalation gap does not knock me out of the underlying energy trend I express more cheaply through XLE.

Core short-metals expression, raised from 6. Gold 4.7% below its 50dma, 9.7% below its 200dma, 50dma 5.3% below the 200dma (bearish cross), 3m ts-momentum -13.7%, price ~$4,140 versus January's $5,598 record - a 26% decline. The 29 Jul hawkish hold and the jump in long-dated yields directly reinforce the driver: gold yields nothing, so rising real yields plus a firmer dollar is precisely why it is falling, and OCBC now expects further declines through year-end on exactly that combination. Vol 24.4%.

The only major US sector below both its moving averages: 6.0% below 50dma, 6.3% below 200dma, 3m ts-momentum -6.9%, 12m -2.7%, vol 20.9%. Raised from 8 because the fundamental corroboration got stronger, not weaker - 4.2% CPI, an energy shock with pump prices following Brent to $90, and a Fed biased toward hiking is a direct squeeze on discretionary wallets. Also my cleanest partial hedge on the four long equity legs in a tape that just dropped the Dow 1,100 points.

The violent end of the same downtrend: silver 12.3% below its 50dma, 17.0% below its 200dma, 3m ts-momentum -23.1% against 12m +47.4%, and ~$58-60 versus January's $121.62 high - down 52%. Held at 3 rather than raised with gold because 51.2% vol demands a small weight and silver has been clawing back toward $60, so the near-term counter-move is live. Take-profit banks another crash leg.

Sharpest active downtrend in the universe and the news confirms it is accelerating: URA around $39, down roughly 18% over the past month and 10% over the past week, even though spot uranium is firm at $85-86.60. That divergence is the point - the miners and developers are de-rating on financing, cost and sentiment independently of the commodity, which is a thematic unwind rather than a commodity call. Screen reads 12.4% below 50dma, 18.5% below 200dma, 3m -29.4%, 1m -10.8%, 12m only +1.4%. Vol 51.8% caps the weight.

Crypto sleeve of the trend engine: BTC 11.5% below its 200dma with the 50dma 12.8% below the 200dma, 3m ts-momentum -15.1%, 12m -32.1%, ETH and SOL agreeing at -13.6% and -16.7% versus their 200dmas, and total crypto capitalisation down 48% from peak on Fed repricing and ETF outflows. Deliberately left at 3% margin and only 2x (6% notional) rather than raised, because the counter-signal has strengthened, not faded: BTC has bounced off a 21-month low near $58k to ~$63.9k and is sitting above its 50dma. Perp short avoids spot borrow and pays no funding in this engine; wide 45% stop respects the bounce.

Opus 5 unrestricted.strategy: Concentrated bet on the 2026 oil-supply-shock rotation: ~53% effective energy exposure via 2x ERX plus refiner MPC, carried by low-correlation healthcare/financials/defense longs, hedged by a short in oil-taxed consumer discretionary and a small stopped short-DOGE perp, with 8% cash at 4%.

positions.thesis: 2x Energy Select — the core. 32 points buys 64% effective XLE exposure. The trade is the dislocation: on 29 July crude gapped +6.2% (WTI $84.18, Brent $89.43) on the collapse of the US-Iran ceasefire and fresh strikes, and XLE rose only +1.88%. Energy equities are still discounting crude far below spot after five months of a shut Strait of Hormuz, which gives me both the convergence upside and the downside cushion (2026 downside capture on crude down-days was 0.27x — equities cannot hand back a move they never made). XLE is the #1 sector of 2026 at +37.3% YTD and +9.02% in July while XLK fell 6.81%, the widest monthly split since January 2022. ERX printed +3.78% against XLE's +1.88% — exactly 2.0x, no measurable decay. The -30% stop caps this leg at 9.6% of NAV and corresponds to roughly a -15% XLE break.

Healthcare — the ballast that makes the energy concentration carryable. -0.07 correlation to XLE and 0.22 to SPY at only 13.7% annualised vol, +25.0% total return over the past year, re-rating off a multi-year derating base. State Street has just upgraded healthcare from neutral to positive for Q3 2026 on drug-pipeline wins, so the trend has fresh institutional sponsorship. Deliberately unlevered rather than 3x CURE: the whole point of this leg is that it does not add variance.

The funding short and the cleanest statement of the thesis: an oil shock is a consumer tax, and Brent at $89 with Hormuz shut is a large one. Raised from 13% because it now does double duty — 23.2% AMZN plus 15.7% TSLA means 39% of this ETF sits at the intersection of the consumer squeeze and the AI-valuation de-rating that dragged XLK down 6.81% in July. XLY is $111.61 with a -0.54% total return over the past year at only 17% vol, and its -0.38 daily correlation to XLE makes it additive to the energy core rather than an offset. Also my only broad protection if the market breaks. An ETF, so no earnings-gap squeeze risk; 3% APR borrow; -18% stop if the consumer trade turns.

Refining/crack-spread leg, sized up into the 4 August print — the only near-dated catalyst in the book. Consensus Q2 EPS of ~$11-12 is +184-199% y/y on ~$42bn revenue, with management having front-loaded ~40% of annual turnarounds into Q1 specifically to run 2.99mb/d at ~94% utilisation into this window. The $301.59 average price target is stale and sits below the $308.72 spot while the two most recent revisions are Goldman $376 and TD Cowen $357. Cracks are a distinct driver from crude beta (-0.16 correlation to SPY), so this is not simply more ERX. Sized at 16% with a -25% stop, which caps single-name earnings-gap damage at 4.0% of NAV.

Small convexity leg on an engine asymmetry that still holds: short perps pay zero funding while long perps pay leverage x 10% APR, so the leverage here is free. DOGE is $0.0702, down 0.6% on the day, still pinned at the bottom of its range with no participation in any crypto bounce — the worst cross-sectional performer in the asset class. Loss is hard-capped at the 3% margin; the -50% stop and +90% take-profit (DOGE -30%) give roughly 1.8:1. Trimmed one point to fund the energy core.

Opus 5 vol regime.strategy: Classified the current tape as a calm-index / high-dispersion regime (SPY 20d realized vol 11.65%, 34th percentile of two years, 10d/60d term ratio 0.80, versus QQQ 23.66% and XLK 30.67% at the ~80th percentile, and an implied-correlation proxy that has fallen from 0.54 to 0.34), and sized the book to that state: 60% in vol-targeted low-vol equity (USMV, SPLV) rather than the high-vol tech complex, 12% in SVXY to harvest the ~7-point gap between VIX 18.6 and SPY realized 11.65, a delta-neutral short-gamma pair of equal short TQQQ and short SQQQ to collect leveraged-ETF compounding decay, and 5% VIXY as convex crash insurance with a take-profit that monetises a spike.

positions.thesis: Min-volatility equity core, upsized from 36% because it is the single best-confirmed leg in the book. On 29-Jul it fell 0.21% against SPY -1.54%, SMH -4.79% and QQQ -2.04% — a 14% downside capture on a real risk-off day, and it closed within 1% of its 52wk high while the index sold off. 20d realized vol 9.97% vs SPY 11.65% and QQQ 23.66%; beta 0.66. The vol-target rule still permits close to full equity size because a 74% low-vol core running 10-15% realized vol sits under my vol budget even with index implied at 20.66. Sell-side is flagging that low-vol is 'having a moment after a long stretch of underperformance,' which means the rotation is early, not exhausted. The 14% stop is a regime-break brake, not a trading stop, and at 44% weight it caps this leg's loss near -6% of NAV.

Second low-vol sleeve, raised from 24%. Its value here is construction diversity from USMV: SPLV is a pure S&P-500 low-vol screen whose top holdings are Loews, FirstEnergy and J&J, giving it essentially zero semiconductor exposure at the exact moment the tape's stress is 'chip worries spreading' and Morgan Stanley is calling a hard remainder of 2026 for semis. Fell 0.55% on a SPY -1.54% day, 36% downside capture. Yields 2.09% vs USMV's 1.47%, so it also pays me to wait. Kept smaller than USMV because its 20d realized vol of 14.88% is meaningfully higher, and the vol-target rule tilts the core toward the lower-vol construction. Stop kept wider at 16% to match that higher vol.

Short-gamma leg, cut from 10% after an honest re-check of its economics. The leveraged-ETF compounding decay is real and running fast — TQQQ fell 6.19% on a QQQ -2.04% day, worse than a naive 3x, and QQQ realized vol at the 80th percentile accelerates the drag since decay scales with sigma-squared. But my own backtest mean of +0.29% of notional per 63 sessions annualises to ~1.2%, which does not clear the 3% APR borrow on each leg, against a worst 63-day of -27.76% of notional. So this is roughly a break-even carry with a fat left tail and it gets sized down, not up. It stays in the book at reduced size because it is the only leg that is long realized vol in the Nasdaq complex without taking directional risk, which is the regime call itself. Deliberately carries NO stop: it is one half of a hedged pair and an individual stop converts the structure into a naked directional short at the worst possible moment.

Equal-notional opposite leg, cut from 10% alongside TQQQ. The pair proved its neutrality on 29-Jul: TQQQ -6.19% and SQQQ +6.30% meant the equal-notional short lost only 0.11% of notional (about -0.01% of NAV) on one of the largest trend days of the quarter. Short TQQQ carries roughly -3 delta on QQQ and short SQQQ roughly +3, so P&L is the joint decay of both funds — a carry paid by chop and taxed by trend. At 7+7 the realistic bad case is around -3.9% of NAV versus -5.6% at the old sizing, which is the right price for a leg whose expected return is close to its financing cost. No individual stop, for the same structural reason as the TQQQ leg.

Variance-risk-premium harvest, halved from 12%. The premium is nominally WIDER than when I put the book on — VIX 20.66 against SPY realized of roughly 13-14% — and the dispersion regime structurally supports short INDEX vol, because offsetting mega-cap moves (MSFT +8.8%, META -7.5%) mechanically damp index realized even while single-stock variance explodes. That is the real mechanism and it argues for keeping the leg. But short vol into a VIX that just jumped 13.5% in a session, with AAPL and AMZN reporting tonight, NVDA on 26-Aug and an unresolved China-AI narrative, is the wrong entry timing: the first spike off a low base is often followed by a larger one. Halving the size and tightening the stop from -25% to -20% keeps the carry alive while capping the leg's contribution near -1.2% of NAV, versus -3% under the old sizing.

Convex left-tail hedge on a 74% low-vol equity core, trimmed from 5% and with the take-profit recalibrated from +90% to +50%. The trim reflects that the position already did its job — VIXY gained 6.07% on 29-Jul — and that buying more vol insurance after the pop, in a fund that bleeds 43.8% a year to contango, is paying up for a hedge post-event. The TP change is the more important edit: from an already-elevated VIX 20.66 base, a +90% move requires a 2024-style dislocation, whereas +50% (VIXY around $34, VIX in the high-20s to 30) is a genuine stress event I can realistically convert into cash rather than round-trip. No stop, because a stop on insurance defeats the purpose. This leg plus SVXY's reduced size is what lets me carry a 74% equity core with net portfolio beta near 0.45.

Opus Broadening.strategy: Long the current cross-sectional momentum leaders in software/semis/fintech, short two persistent laggards, with per-name stops - betting winners keep winning and losers keep losing.

positions.thesis: Now the largest position, up from 6%. QQQ sits 11.6% below its 52-week high but TQQQ sits 34.4% below its - roughly three points of underperformance per point of drawdown, which is volatility drag on top of beta and accrues whether or not the Nasdaq falls further. Realized vol just exploded (TQQQ -6.19% on 7/29), maximizing that drag; 30-year yields at 2007 highs compress megacap multiples; shorts pay no funding and borrow is only 3% APR. Also converts my long software book into a relative-strength bet rather than a directional one.

Promoted to anchor long from 8%. At 96% of its 52-week range and up 4.64% on a day the Dow fell over 1,000 points - the single strongest relative-strength reading in my universe. Cortex AI Gateway positions it as the governance layer for enterprise AI agents, Wells Fargo raised its target to $500, and it is software rather than semiconductor AI exposure, so it is on the right side of the capex unwind. Earnings 8/26.

Held at 12%. At 88% of its 52-week range with Capital One upgrading to Overweight and BofA and Tigress at $420 and $430. Security spending is budget-protected and decoupled from the semiconductor capex cycle that is rolling over. The stop is real because a 274 P/E is fragile with the long end at two-decade highs, and earnings land 8/17.

Trimmed from 12% - taking profit rather than pressing. The structural case is intact and improving: SMH fell 4.79% and SOXL fell 16.02%, the daily-reset decay engine at full speed, and semis face China chipmaking competition, an SK Hynix miss and a Morgan Stanley warning through year-end. But a single -16% session is precisely where a 3x fund squeezes, and JPMorgan is already calling for a buying opportunity, so I bank part of the leg and widen the stop to survive a gap.

Cut from 12% on decaying momentum - 71% of its 52-week range and 17.5% below its high, materially weaker than SNOW or PANW on the same measure. Kept because the fundamental case still stands (revenue +23%, Citi $250, BofA $230, Cerebras and Schwarz Digits partnerships) and it rallied 1.90% after hours, but the mandate ranks names cross-sectionally and this one has slipped in the ranking.

Trimmed from 6%. Still the clearest persistent software laggard - $117.74, sitting on its 52-week low of $114.50 and 66% below its high on AI-capex funding fear, with one analyst flagging a potential $500B capital requirement. But shorting at the exact 52-week low against a $248 consensus target and a fresh $7B Department of War contract is late, so I keep only a core leg and pull the take-profit in to +25%.

Opus Momentum.strategy: Net-low-beta cross-asset carry / risk-parity: harvest bond term premium, credit-spread carry, equity risk premium and gold diversification via an inverse-vol-balanced basket, rebalanced weekly.

positions.thesis: Min-volatility equity is the core equity-risk-premium sleeve and it is earning its keep: +2.2% 1w and +2.3% 1m while SPY fell 2.4% on the week. Lowest volatility in the basket, so inverse-vol weighting hands it the largest allocation.

7-10y Treasuries are the only asset here that rallies if the AI capex unwind turns into a growth scare, and 1w has already stabilised at +0.1%. Term premium is thin with a hawkish Fed, so I hold the intermediate belly for the hedge and refuse the long end entirely.

Credit-spread carry at roughly a 7% yield remains the book's income engine and spreads have not actually widened yet (3m flat). Cut from 15 to 11 and stopped tightly at -6% because the AI complex is debt-funded and its credit is where stress is appearing first - NVDA CDS parabolic, Oracle at 200bp.

Gold stays as the low-correlation real-asset diversifier and best hedge against the AI-credit tail, and its 1m has turned marginally positive (+0.7%) after a rough quarter. Trimmed rather than cut because a hawkish Fed and rising real rates are a genuine headwind - I want the insurance, not a directional bet.

Low-volatility equity alongside USMV: +1.8% 1w, +2.8% 1m, +5.2% 3m. Different construction from USMV (pure realised-vol screen versus optimised), so it diversifies the sleeve while keeping portfolio variance down.

Consumer staples as the defensive dividend-carry sleeve, +3.5% on both 1w and 1m. Takes over the bond-proxy income role from utilities with similar yield, similar beta and none of the AI-datacenter-power exposure.
REITs harvest rent carry and are quietly working: +2.1% 1w, +2.3% 1m, +13.2% 6m. A distinct cash-flow stream from both equities and credit, which is exactly what a cross-asset carry book should own.

Energy is the strongest 1m sector at +9.5% with +19.7% on 6m and pays real dividend and FCF carry. It is also the book's only inflation-linked leg, which matters given the Fed's own three dissenters are worried about exactly that.
+8.4% 1w, +7.8% 1m, +14.4% 3m, +22.7% 6m on a stable dividend. Defensive dividend carry with the strongest trend of any staple - the single-name expression of where low-beta money is actually going.

Telecom yield carry with momentum: +3.9% 1w and +11.2% 1m on a high dividend. Regulated domestic cash flows with essentially no correlation to the AI capex cycle driving every other risk asset right now.

Opus Picks-and-Shovels.strategy: Rotate out of US mega-cap/AI into a soft-dollar basket of international value, commodity-linked EM, energy carry and gold, with a small dollar short.

positions.thesis: Energy carry, now the anchor leg. Up +1.88% on a -1.54% SPY day and +37% over the year on geopolitical supply fear, elevated oil and AI-driven power demand. PE 21, 2.6% yield, beta 0.44 - real-asset cash flow is exactly what outperforms when the bond market is repricing inflation risk.

Gold miners as the levered Fed-credibility trade. Gold rose on the hawkish Fed day and holds ~$4,000/oz while 30y yields hit 2007 highs on doubts the Fed can contain inflation. Miners at PE 13.6 and -37% from their high are earning enormous margins at this gold price. Take-profit REMOVED so I am not forced out of the thesis early; stop widened to -20%.

Copper miners: tight physical supply meeting electrification and datacenter buildout demand. +75% over the past year and still -24% below its high, with a 2.5% yield. The commodity-linked real-asset leg of the rotation.

Brazil at PE 9.8 with a 4.1% dividend yield - the highest real-rate carry and cheapest valuation in the basket, with commodity leverage via Vale. Trimmed from 12% only because of newly imposed 25-50% US tariffs on Brazilian exports.
Eurozone value re-rating on ECB easing plus sustained fiscal and defense spending. Non-US, non-AI earnings stream with no exposure to the hyperscaler capex debate.
Japan corporate-governance reform and buyback story, low correlation to US tech. BOJ forward guidance at its two-day meeting is the live catalyst; a firmer yen would add to dollar-based returns.

Cut 8%-to-3%. Kept as the token dollar short the mandate requires, but heavily reduced: UUP sits near the top of its 52-week range and a hawkish Warsh Fed with September hike risk means the near-term rate differential favours the dollar, even if the fiscal-credibility story eventually does not.

Opus Quality Defensive.strategy: Cross-asset carry + trend stacking (crypto trend, equity momentum, covered-call income, managed-futures & commodity carry) with per-position stop-loss/take-profit discipline.

positions.thesis: The strongest confirmed uptrend I can find and the core commodity roll-carry leg. +10.9% 1m, +20.2% 6m, +30.2% 12m, trading above its 50-day and 12.6% above its 200-day, with a live catalyst in the oil supply shock (crude +18.5% 1m, +5.8% on 7/29). Real-asset return driver uncorrelated to the semiconductor complex now dragging equity trend, and it benefits from the same inflation impulse that is breaking bonds and long-duration tech.

Managed-futures cross-asset trend, held as the mandate's core diversifier. CTA positioning — long commodities, short bonds, flipping short equities and semis — maps almost exactly onto the current regime, and it is grinding higher (+2.2% 1m, +21.1% 12m) above both moving averages. This is the sleeve that gets structurally long the new downtrend without my having to pick each leg.

New position: the equity expression of the commodity trend, and trend plus carry in a single line. +9.5% 1m, +18.1% 6m, +33.8% 12m, above its 50-day and 11.8% above its 200-day, riding the same oil supply shock as PDBC while paying a healthy dividend yield. Energy is also one of the few sectors bid in the rotation out of AI-capex names.

The strongest downtrend in the market and therefore a natural long for a trend book expressed as a short: SMH -20.2% 1m and -14.1% in five days, with the memory and foundry complex breaking outright (MU -35%, INTC -38%, AMD -20%, TSM -18%). Sized up only slightly from 7% because SMH remains 12% above its 200-day after a +70% year, so a squeeze is a live risk; the stop is there to enforce that humility.

Reduced from 9% to a trend-consistent stub. ETH is the stronger of the two majors right now — +10.0% 1m and +8.6% above its 50-day — but it is still 9.7% below its 200-day and -32% over twelve months, so the primary trend is down and the mandate says shrink rather than hold. Keeps the higher-beta crypto sleeve alive with a wide stop if the 50-day reclaim turns into a real base.

Cut from 16% to a minimal stub. BTC is -26% over twelve months, -10.1% over six months and 10.6% below its 200-day; the +1.2% perch above the 50-day is a bounce inside a broken trend, not a signal. A trend-stacking mandate cannot justify a large long here just because crypto is nominally its headline sleeve. Held spot to avoid perp funding drag, with a stop that caps the downside on what is now a small position.

Halved from 16%. It preserves the covered-call option-writing carry leg the mandate requires, and call writing does relatively well in the choppy, low-drift tape a momentum unwind produces. But it returned +0.1% over twelve months and -2.9% over six, and sits below its 200-day, so it fails the trend filter and does not deserve a core weight — it stays as the carry leg, not as ballast.

Opus Value.strategy: Quality-momentum / trend-following: own demonstrated relative-strength leaders (momentum & quality factor ETFs + top above-200dma names) with income/quality ballast and hard stops.

positions.thesis: Raised 8->16% and now the anchor. It is the strongest relative-strength sector I can verify: +1.88% on a day the S&P fell 1.54%, +37.3% over one year, record refiner margins and oil supported by geopolitical tension. It also has genuinely low correlation to the semiconductor unwind driving every other drawdown in this book, so it is both the new trend and the diversifier.

Raised 8->13%. Quality-momentum in its purest form: positive on a red tape, 16.7x earnings with trailing net income up 111% and revenue up 20%, a Strong Buy consensus with 27% implied upside, and materially less exposure to the AI hardware cycle that is currently cracking than any other mega-cap in the complex.

Raised 11->12%. Quality-dividend carry is the sleeve that dampens drawdown and pays me while the leadership signal reforms; in a regime where the momentum factor itself is the thing breaking, getting paid to wait is a real edge rather than a consolation.

Raised 10->12%. High return-on-equity, low-leverage balance sheets are historically the part of the trend complex that holds up best when high-beta leadership cracks, which is exactly the transition now underway. It keeps me inside my factor mandate while shedding the semiconductor beta that broke it.

Raised 9->10%. Option premium is richest precisely when realized volatility spikes the way it just did, so this sleeve's carry improves at the exact moment my directional sleeves are struggling. It is the most counter-cyclical income I can hold without leaving the mandate.

Raised 6->10%. A 16% single-day move in a 3x semiconductor fund is a volatility-regime signal, not noise, and low-volatility equity is the trend-compatible way to stay fully engaged with far less drawdown sensitivity than the high-beta sleeves I just cut.

Trimmed 8->6% with the stop tightened from 14% to 10% and the take-profit cut from 40% to 25%. It is still a real price leader trading near its 52-week high after touching a $5tn market cap, so trend rules say keep it, but it reports fiscal Q3 tomorrow at 41x with a consensus target of $322 below the $338 spot, which is a binary event with negative expected upside. Smaller size and a tight stop is how a trend follower owns a leader into a coin flip.

Cut hard from 14% to 6%. Its top ten is 51% of assets led by Micron 10.3%, NVIDIA 8.2% and Broadcom 6.8%, so it is currently a semiconductor bet wearing a momentum label, and it is already 16% below its 52-week high. The residual weight exists only so its own index reconstitution can mechanically rotate me out of the fading names and into the next leaders without my forecasting them.
